Florida accuses Meta of deliberately designing its platforms to be addictive for young users and misleading consumers about safety measures. Florida argues that the settlement is insufficient. $META

Google launched SynthID in 2023 to watermark AI-generated media with imperceptible signals. The company says it has watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos, along with 240,000 years of audio content. A preview of the detector was previously available to media professionals. The tool expands Google’s existing verification features across Search, Gemini and Chrome, which collectively handle more than 1 million verification requests per day. Developed by Google DeepMind, the global rollout aims to give consumers broader access to tools for identifying AI-generated content online. $GOOGL

"The differences in p-values presented by us and by the FDA… are more a result of disease heterogeneity and the sample size." 0.045 vs 0.21 is a precision problem, not a signal problem. items.content_excerpt: $AXSM I've been looking more closely at the Auvelity weekly IQVIA numbers, and I'm actually a little less concerned about the raw numbers than I was, although there is still a significant question that needs answering. Through the first 12 weeks of Q3, IQVIA shows 239,600 Auvelity TRx versus 216,648 during the first 12 weeks of Q2. That's about 10.6% sequential growth. In fact, Q3 has already exceeded the entire Q2 IQVIA total of 235,448 with one week still remaining. So Auvelity isn't really flat quarter over quarter. The bigger question is why we aren't seeing more acceleration considering the ADA launch and the substantially expanded sales force. One thing that stands out when looking at the historical data is the difference between IQVIA prescriptions and the numbers Axsome ultimately reports. In Q2, IQVIA showed 235,448 TRx while Axsome reported approximately 266,000. That means IQVIA captured only about 88.5% of the company-reported number. (Continued)
